question: If b sin θ = a, then sec θ + tan θ = ?
solution:
**Given:**

b sin θ= a

**Concept used:**

sinθ = Perpendicular/ Hypotenuse

secθ = Hypotenuse/ Base

tanθ = Perpendicular/ Base

**Calculation:**

bsinθ = a

sinθ = a/b

So, Perpendicular = a & Hypotenuse = b

(Hypotenuse)² = (Perpendicular)² + (Base)²

b² = a²+ Base²

base² = b²- a²

base = {√{b²-a²} }

secθ = Hypotenuse/ base= b/{ √{b²-a²} }

tanθ= perpendicular/ base= a/{ √{b²-a²} }

So, secθ+ tanθ = b/{ √{b²-a²} }+ (a/{ √{b²-a²} })

secθ + tanθ = (b+ a)/({ √{b²-a²} })

∵ (b + a) = √(b + a) × √(b + a) 

⇒ secθ + tanθ = {√{(b+a)(b+a)} }/ { √{(b-a)(b+a)} }

**secθ+ tanθ= √ {frac{{b + a}}{{b - a}}} **
